newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Viasa workers reject emergency plan.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Viasa workers reject emergency plan.

text.p: The future of loss-making Venezuelan airline Viasa was thrown in doubt Thursday with the rejection of a restructuring plan by the company's workers.
Viasa 2,200 employees, grouped in five unions, said the plan was "not viable" because it failed to "guarantee the future of the company next year," union leader William Bracho said.
He spoke to reporters after a meeting between Viasa management, workers' delegates and representatives of Spanish airline Iberia, which owns 45 percent of Viasa.

Viasa shareholders have said they want a radical restructuring of Venezuela's flag carrier airline to be implemented before January 15. Viasa's losses have totaled $200 million in the past five years.
The plan involves cutting 380 jobs, freezing pay and shedding unprofitable routes.
Employees have proposed to seek fresh investors in order to recapitalize the company but Bracho said "the management is unwilling to let new investors in."
Iberia executive Javier Alvarez argued that before opening up the capital Viasa "had first to be made profitable."
Iberia invested an initial $73.5 million to buy its stake in Viasa in 1991 and another $43.6 million later to cover losses and is therefore unwilling to stump up further capital.

The Venezuelan government, which owns 40 percent of the airline through the Venezuelan Investment Fund (FIV), has warned that failure to adopt the restructuring plan could lead to the company being unable to operate beyond end-January.
